title: Learning from failure: own failures vs. shared failures
html:
Learning from failure: own failures vs. shared failures

Question: Does making failed attempts public help, and under which rules?

Answer: Best: OSO, learn from own, 8.0 (1 more tie). Best traditional: Traditional, learn from all (public), 7.6. Clear difference.

Traditional no learning 5.7 ± 1.2 0.35 96 ± 16 0.22 ± 0.18
Traditional learn from own 7.4 ± 0.7 0.96 87 ± 17 0.70 ± 0.35
Traditional learn from all (public) 7.6 ± 0.6 0.98 82 ± 17 0.88 ± 0.35
OSO (immediate) no learning 7.9 ± 0.2 1.00 49 ± 14 1.44 ± 0.48
OSO (immediate) learn from own 8.0 ± 0.0 1.00 37 ± 10 2.16 ± 0.62
OSO (immediate) learn from all (public) 8.0 ± 0.0 1.00 29 ± 6 2.99 ± 0.63

Design (fixed before the run): compared own failures or shared failures, under each rule setting · held the same: the Lean tree, agents and budget · measure: hardest level published, higher is better · 100 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

With the learning oracle, each failed attempt raises the next chance on that idea by 10% of p. With rules.publishFailures, failed attempts are public, so agents also learn from others' failures (sharedWeight = 1). Compared under traditional and OSO (immediate) rules on the default world.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
